**US stocks in play — 2026-11-05 (open digest)**

- **Run time:** the **09:50 ET** fire (Thu 2026-11-05, a normal trading day — not an exchange holiday; next NYSE closure 2026-11-26).
- **This artifact is a RECONSTRUCTION of the 09:50 ET session state, not a live print.** The platform resumed this conversation in place at **10:38 ET** ,
- so every price, volume and pace number below is rebuilt from Yahoo 5-minute bars **as they stood at 09:50 ET** ,
- and the catalysts were verified at run time (10:38 ET).
- The `chg @ 10:25 ET` column carries the live path since 09:50 so the reader can see what the 09:50 snapshot missed.
- **Session state:** US cash session **OPEN** at the fire instant.
- **The gap verdicts cover only the first ~20 minutes (09:30 → 09:50 ET)** — `held` here means **"the gap held for 20 minutes"**, NOT "held into the bell".
- The pre-close fire at 15:50 ET owns the rest of the session.
- **Slot:** `open`. The deployed schedule (`50 9,15 * * 1-5`) determines the slot, so the **open** floors apply:
- price ≥ $1, market cap ≥ $50m (soft), **session $ volume ≥ ~$0.5m to 09:50**, and the **pace** measure instead of RVol.
- **Sort note:** Tier A → Soft-A → TECH_WATCH → B → C.
- **Within each tier, ranked by session USD dollar volume to 09:50 descending.** TECH_WATCH here means *no same-session company catalyst but trading on size* (pace ≥ 1.0);
- Tier B is *a move without a catalyst on sub-normal pace*.
- **Prior digest:** **there is no prior open board** —
- `us-stocks-in-play/` holds no `-open.md` file for any earlier date, so the routine has **no `changed_since` delta to publish** and this is the **first link in the open-board chain**.
- The **Overnight → open** annex below substitutes for it: it loads the `overnight_carry` from the **2026-11-04 pre-close board** (`us-stocks-in-play/2026-11-04.md`) and reports which of those names are in play this morning.
- **Universe scanned:** **6,091 US cash-venue equities** (NASDAQ / NYSE / AMEX, `type` in (stock, dr)), of which **5,569** trade above $1.
- The trigger sets were pulled in **six single atomic TradingView scan calls** (`chg ≥ 3%` 341, `chg ≤ -3%` 1,399, `gap ≥ 2%` 491, `gap ≤ -2%` 637, `volume ≥ 750k` 631, `RVol ≥ 1.2` 185), **each verified against its own `totalCount`** —
- a paginated pull of the same universe silently lost nine large names (ARM, QCOM, SWKS, STX, WDC, TER, ON, LITE, DRVN) on the first attempt, so the atomic-call rule was applied.
- Their union was **2,437** names, plus 27 majors and carry names = **2,464 candidates priced**; **2,328 priced successfully** (136 Yahoo 404s on dead symbols).
- **At the 09:50 ET trigger** (`|chg| ≥ 3%` **or** `|gap| ≥ 3%`) **1,524 names survived** — 667 on the gap leg, 857 on the move leg —
- and **after the floors 944 remained** (131 of them in the $0.5–1m dollar-volume band). **All 944 are priced and tiered; there is no top-N cap and no unpriced tail.**
- **Pace basis:** `pace = (session volume to 09:50 ÷ trailing-10 FULL-session average volume) ÷ 0.125`.
- The denominator is the **trailing 10 settled sessions ending 2026-11-04** (2026-10-22 → 2026-11-04), computed market-wide from `polygon-io grouped_daily` in 11 calls.
- The numerator is the Yahoo 5-minute series, which for the same symbol on the same session sums to a **median 0.893 of its own daily bar** (per-symbol factor, winsorised to 0.40–1.60) —
- that factor is applied so the numerator sits on the same daily-bar basis as the denominator.
- **Two independent checks:** the polygon denominator agrees with Yahoo's own trailing-10 daily average to a **median 0.029%** (p95 0.28%), and the resulting pace **rank-correlates 0.951 (Spearman) with the TradingView scanner's live RVol** across 783 names.

**The headline**

- **The AI pause got a second day, and this time it was the memory complex that broke.** Yesterday's post-election rotation was a thesis de-rate; overnight it became a **policy headline**.
- On the night of 2026-11-04, **Rep.
- Yassamin Ansari (D-AZ)** posted on X that *"Top of the Democratic agenda on day 1 needs to be a pause on advanced AI development, regulation of this out of control industry, and a ban on artificial superintelligence."* That is a direct threat to the data-centre build-out that the memory and storage names' record quarters were built on, and at 09:50 ET the tape was pricing exactly that:
- **SNDK -13.20% on $4.09bn in twenty minutes, MU -9.03% on $7.48bn (the largest dollar volume on the board), WDC -11.81%, STX -11.71%, SKHY (SK hynix ADR) -8.19%** —
- and then it spread into the rest of the AI complex, with **AMD -11.05%**, **TSM -5.98%**, **AVGO -5.01%**, **ARM -9.16%**, **QCOM -8.90%**, **MRVL -8.59%**, **PANW -8.94%**, **PLTR -7.75%** and the neoclouds (**CRWV -7.34%**, **NBIS -11.47%**, **IREN -9.65%**, **VRT -10.24%**, **CIFR -9.15%**).
- **The index split is the story:
- the Nasdaq-100 -3.22% against the Dow -0.43% and the S&P -1.40%**, with **XLK -4.15% and SMH -6.03%** versus **XLE +1.21%, XLF +0.47%, XLV +0.62%, XLP +1.04%, XLU +0.64%** —
- the second day of the blue-wave rotation, now with a policy mechanism instead of just a thesis.

- The caveat that changes how this should be read:
- **this is still a policy headline, not a fundamental verdict, and the tape kept deteriorating after the snapshot.** At 09:50 the S&P was -1.40% with the **VIX +20.35% to 19.99**;
- by the last bar of the pull (**~10:25 ET**) the S&P ETF was **-2.18%**, the Nasdaq-100 ETF **-4.31%**, **SMH -7.76%** and the **VXX +15.33%**.
- The vol is the tell — a vol shock plus a lower 10-year (**4.882%, -1.2bp**) is a de-rating tape, not a rotation tape.
- And the second caveat is that **the memory names were already the cheapest they had ever been**:
- Micron closed yesterday at $795.23 after a -7.0% day with its data-centre revenue narrative intact, and SanDisk printed a beat-and-raise on Oct-29;
- today the policy headline hit names whose forward multiples were already at multi-year lows. **If the pause language does not become legislation, the de-rate is as reversible as yesterday's was.**

- There are only **two genuine same-session prints on the whole board**, and they point in opposite directions.
- **APP +30.49%** on a Q3 beat with pre-open price-target raises (Jefferies $430, Scotiabank $450, BTIG $450) —
- **$3.92bn of turnover in twenty minutes, a pace of 17.9**, and the biggest single-name event of the morning.
- And **U (Unity) +12.13%** (gap +18.64%, pace 13.3) on a Q3 2026 beat with a robust Q4 outlook.
- Everything else on the board is either a **policy/theme move** or a **single-stock earnings collapse**:
- **MNTN -51.49%** (Q3 revenue hit by a sales-force shake-up, Raymond James downgrade), **VCYT -56.68%** (Decipher Prostate volume miss, 2027 growth outlook reset to mid-single-digit, Leerink downgrade, Needham PT $69 → $46) and **MELI -13.01%** (Q3 profit miss on free-shipping costs).

**Method and caveats**

- **Every number is a 09:50 ET reconstruction, not a live print.** The conversation was resumed at 10:38 ET.
- Prices, session volumes, gaps and pace are rebuilt from 5-minute bars at the 09:50 cut; catalysts were verified at run time.
- The `chg @ 10:25 ET` column is the last 5-minute bar available when the screen was pulled —
- the selloff deepened (S&P ETF -1.41% → -2.18%, SMH -6.03% → -7.76%) after the snapshot.
- **The gap verdicts cover 20 minutes, not the session.** `held` = "held for 20 minutes".
- The pre-close fire at 15:50 ET owns the held-into-the-bell question, and its gap annex is a different screen with a different floor.
- **The pace measure is a screening measure, not a measurement.** The 0.125 opening-share constant is regime-dependent (the skill's own measurement put the daily median between 10.77% and 16.49%), and **pace is not comparable with the pre-close slot's RVol** —
- the column is labelled `pace` everywhere, including in the CSV.
- The Yahoo 5-minute series is reconciled to each symbol's own daily bar by a **per-symbol factor measured on the prior session** (median 0.893);
- the residual risk is that the missing 10.7% of volume is not perfectly proportional through the day, so a single name's pace can carry **±20%** of error.
- The rank correlation with an independent daily-basis volume measure (TradingView's live RVol) is **0.951**, which is the strongest available evidence that the *ordering* is sound.
- **Screen completeness:** the trigger sets were pulled atomically and verified against their own `totalCount` after a paginated pull silently dropped nine large names.
- **The 09:50 move trigger itself carries one honest hole**:
- a name that was more than 3% *at 09:50* but was flat by the time the scanner was pulled at ~11:00 ET, and whose pre-market gap was under 2%, and whose turnover was under 750k shares, would not have entered the candidate set —
- it would have to have been found by name. Everything that gapped ≥ 2% or was moving ≥ 3% at run time, or traded 750k+ shares, **is** in the set.
- **The gap column disagrees with TradingView's pre-market change by more than 2pp on 72 of 845 names** (a median 0.083pp).
- Those names are flagged `unverified` rather than dropped, and the digest's gap numbers are the Yahoo bar series throughout — one source per field.
- **Not verified:** the proximate cause of **AEHL +74.00%**, **ARQ +33.24%**, **ZNB +79.05%**, **FLYE +38.24%** and **ELPW +56.77%** could not be confirmed with a dated source;
- those names are published with the price, the float and no catalyst claim.
- **TSLA -8.90%** and **COHR -8.44%** carry a positive same-session print against a negative tape and are labelled that way.
- **BE -14.60%** has no same-session catalyst located before the 09:50 cut (the NTT DATA 900 MW announcement is timestamped 10:00 ET, after the snapshot).
- **The fuel log's `errors` count is the number of degraded sources, not the number of failed symbols.** The 136 Yahoo 404s are dead symbols that were already excluded by the universe, and are not counted as source errors.

- **degraded_sources: 3** — (1) the TradingView scanner's `halted` column is null on every row, so **the halt trigger could not be evaluated** this session;
- (2) the shared pre-open feed's **catalyst column was unusable for every name** ("no catalyst captured at this checkpoint"), so the verdicts here are **bar-derived only**;
- (3) the **gap field is `unverified` for 72 of 845 names** (>2pp disagreement between the two independent pre-market sources).
